{{short description|None}}
{{Figure skating records and statistics}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=February 2025}}
[[Figure skating at the Olympic Games|Figure skating has been part of the Olympic Games]] since [[figure skating at the 1908 Summer Olympics|1908]] and has been contested at 26 Olympic Games. There have been 301 medals (101 gold, 100 silver, and 100 bronze) awarded to figure skaters representing 30 [[National Olympic Committee]]s. Six events have been contested, but one, men's [[special figures]], was discontinued after a single Olympics. 

Canadian ice dancers [[Tessa Virtue]] and [[Scott Moir]] are the only figure skaters to win five Olympic medals (three gold medals and two silver medals). Swedish figure skater [[Gillis Grafström]], Russian figure skater [[Evgeni Plushenko]], and Japanese figure skaters [[Yuma Kagiyama]] and [[Kaori Sakamoto]] have each won four medals. The only skaters with three consecutive titles are Grafström in men's singles, [[Sonja Henie]] for Norway in women's singles, and [[Irina Rodnina]] from the Soviet Union in pair skating. Americans [[Nathan Chen]] and [[Alysa Liu]], along with Canadians Tessa Virtue and Scott Moir, are the only skaters to win two gold medals in the same Olympics. {{clear}}

=== Men's special figures ===
Men's [[special figures]] was only included in one Olympic Games before being discontinued. The sole winner of the event was Russian [[Nikolai Panin]], who gave his country its first ever Olympic gold medal.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Windhausen |first=John D. |year=1976 |title=Russia's First Olympic Victor |journal=Journal of Sport History |publisher=North American Society for Sport History |volume=3 |issue=1 |pages=35–44 |url=http://www.la84foundation.org/SportsLibrary/JSH/JSH1976/JSH0301/jsh0301d.pdf|access-date=July 15, 2009 |archive-date=August 7, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100807185857/http://www.la84foundation.org/SportsLibrary/JSH/JSH1976/JSH0301/jsh0301d.pdf |url-status=dead}}</ref>

=== Pairs ===
At the 1964 Olympics, [[Marika Kilius]] and [[Hans-Jürgen Bäumler]] of Germany, [[Debbi Wilkes]] and [[Guy Revell]] of Canada, and [[Vivian Joseph]] and [[Ronald Joseph (figure skater)|Ronald Joseph]] of the United States placed second, third, and fourth, respectively. Two years later, Kilius and Bäumler's results were invalidated because the pair had signed a professional contract before the Olympics. The silver medals were re-allocated to Wilkes and Revell and the bronze medals to Joseph and Joseph. However, in 1987, the German team was re-awarded their silver medals after an appeal. In November 2014, the [[International Olympic Committee]] clarified that both the German and Canadian teams were the silver medalists, and the U.S. team were the bronze medalists.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://web.icenetwork.com/news/2014/11/25/102439578/ | title = Fifty years later, Joseph siblings find redemption | work = IceNetwork.com | date = November 25, 2014 | access-date = November 28, 2014 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20141129185254/http://web.icenetwork.com/news/2014/11/25/102439578 | archive-date = November 29, 2014 | url-status = dead | df = mdy-all }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Hersh |first=Philip |date=November 25, 2014 |title=A Half-Century Later, Joseph Siblings Recognized as Olympic Medal-Winners |url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/international/ct-figure-skating-spt-1126-20141125-column.html |newspaper=[[Chicago Tribune]] |access-date=November 28, 2014 |archive-date=February 26, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180226134818/http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/international/ct-figure-skating-spt-1126-20141125-column.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

At the [[Figure skating at the 2002 Winter Olympics – Pair skating|2002 Winter Olympics]], a controversy involving allegations of vote swapping and buying of votes of the French judge culminated in the judge's scores being discarded and [[Jamie Salé]] and [[David Pelletier]] of Canada, who had originally finished second, being awarded gold medals, with [[Elena Berezhnaya]] and [[Anton Sikharulidze]] of Russia, who originally finished first, being allowed to keep theirs.<ref name="TMH02162002">{{cite news |last=Robertson|first=Linda|date=February 16, 2002|title=Extra championship medal granted to settle controversy in pairs event|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-miami-herald-extra-championships-med/189662517/|access-date=January 23, 2026|work=[[The Miami Herald]]|pages=[https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-miami-herald-extra-championships-med/189662517/ 1A], [https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-miami-herald-second-gold-medal-grant/189662563/ 14A]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> An arrangement had allegedly been concocted whereby the French judge, [[Marie-Reine Le Gougne]], was to award the gold medal to the Russian pairs team, while the Russian ice dance judge was to award the gold medal to the French ice dance team.<ref name="Guardian050120022">{{cite news |last=Mackay |first=Duncan |date=May 1, 2002 |title=French officials banned over gold scandal |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2002/may/01/olympicgames.winterolympics2002 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140216011053/https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2002/may/01/olympicgames.winterolympics2002 |archive-date=February 16, 2014 |access-date=January 23, 2026 |work=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> In April 2002, the [[International Skating Union]] (ISU) announced that Marie-Reine Le Gougne and [[Didier Gailhaguet]], president of the [[French Federation of Ice Sports]], had both been suspended for three years for their roles in the scandal and also prohibited from any official involvement with the [[2006 Winter Olympics]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Communication No. 1181 |url=http://www.isu.org/vsite/vfile/page/fileurl/0,11040,4844-137120-154336-25640-0-file,00.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090325050602/http://www.isu.org/vsite/vfile/page/fileurl/0,11040,4844-137120-154336-25640-0-file,00.pdf |archive-date=March 25, 2009 |access-date=November 4, 2007}}</ref><ref name="Guardian050120022" />

| {{flagicon|AUT}} [[Innsbruck]]

=== Team event ===
The team event is the newest Olympic figure skating event, first contested in the [[Figure skating at the 2014 Winter Olympics|2014 Games]]. It combines the four [[Figure skating#Olympic disciplines|Olympic figure skating disciplines]] (men's singles, women's singles, pairs, and ice dance) into a single event; gold is awarded to the team that earns the most placement points.

The results of the 2022 team event were fraught with controversy. The medal ceremony originally scheduled for February 8 was delayed over what International Olympic Committee (IOC) spokesperson Mark Adams described as a situation that required "legal consultation" with the International Skating Union.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 9, 2022 |title=Olympic Medals in Team Figure Skating Delayed by Legal Issue |url=https://apnews.com/article/winter-olympics-figure-skating-sports-international-olympic-committee-court-of-arbitration-for-sport-c49077705737be8a7d41a2847c2f355b |access-date=February 9, 2022 |website=[[The Associated Press|AP News]] |language=en |archive-date=February 9, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220209061349/https://apnews.com/article/winter-olympics-figure-skating-sports-international-olympic-committee-court-of-arbitration-for-sport-c49077705737be8a7d41a2847c2f355b |url-status=live }}</ref> Several media outlets reported that the issue was over a positive test from December 2021 that showed the presence of [[trimetazidine]] in a sample given by [[Kamila Valieva]] from the [[Russian Olympic Committee athletes at the 2022 Winter Olympics|Russian Olympic Committee]] (ROC),<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Tétrault-Farber |first1=Gabrielle |last2=Axon |first2=Iain |last3=Grohmann |first3=Karolos |date=February 9, 2022 |title=Figure skating-Russian Media Say Teen Star Tested Positive for Banned Drug |url=https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/figure-skating-medals-ceremony-delayed-over-legal-consultation-2022-02-09/ |access-date=February 9, 2022 |work=[[Reuters]] |language=en |archive-date=February 9, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220209062431/https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/figure-skating-medals-ceremony-delayed-over-legal-consultation-2022-02-09/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Brennan |first=Christine |author-link=Christine Brennan |date=February 9, 2022 |title=Positive Drug Test by Russian Kamila Valieva Has Forced a Delay of Olympic Team Medals Ceremony |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/olympics/beijing/2022/02/09/olympic-figure-skating-team-medals-delayed-russian-drug-test/6717526001/ |website=[[USA Today]] |access-date=May 27, 2023 |archive-date=February 9, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220209113551/https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/olympics/beijing/2022/02/09/olympic-figure-skating-team-medals-delayed-russian-drug-test/6717526001/ |url-status=live }}</ref> which was officially confirmed on February 11. The [[Russian Anti-Doping Agency]] (RUSADA), under suspension from the [[World Anti-Doping Agency]] (WADA) since 2015<ref>{{cite news |last=Faloyin |first=Dipo |date=November 19, 2015 |title=WADA Suspends Russia's Anti-Doping Agency |url=http://europe.newsweek.com/wada-suspends-russias-anti-doping-agency-non-compliance-396283?rm=eu |access-date=February 14, 2022 |work=[[Newsweek]] |archive-date=July 26, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210726114519/http://europe.newsweek.com/wada-suspends-russias-anti-doping-agency-non-compliance-396283?rm=eu |url-status=live }}</ref> for its years of serving solely to hide the positive doping results of Russian athletes,<ref>{{cite news |last=Ford |first=Bonnie D. |date=July 18, 2016 |title=Takeaways from McLaren Report? Confusion, Corruption, Cynicism |url=https://www.espn.com/olympics/story/_/id/17100024/takeaways-mclaren-report-confusion-corruption-cynicism |access-date=February 13, 2022 |work=[[ESPN]] |archive-date=July 24, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160724232925/http://espn.go.com/olympics/story/_/id/17100024/takeaways-mclaren-report-confusion-corruption-cynicism |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Hendricks |first=Maggie |date=July 18, 2016 |title=The Damning McLaren Report on Russian Olympic Doping, Explained |url=http://ftw.usatoday.com/2016/07/the-damning-mclaren-report-on-russian-olympic-doping-explained |access-date=February 13, 2022 |work=[[USA Today]] |archive-date=February 14, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220214044648/https://ftw.usatoday.com/2016/07/the-damning-mclaren-report-on-russian-olympic-doping-explained |url-status=live }}</ref> cleared Valieva on February 9, a day after the December test results were released and two months after the test. The IOC, WADA, and the ISU appealed the RUSADA's decision.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Russian Anti-Doping Agency Allowed Kamila Valieva to Compete in Olympics Despite Failed Drug Test |url=https://www.cnn.com/2022/02/10/sport/kamila-valieva-roc-drugs-test-olympics-spt-intl-hnk/index.html |access-date=February 15, 2022 |website=Cnn.com |date=February 11, 2022 |archive-date=February 14, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220214230148/https://www.cnn.com/2022/02/10/sport/kamila-valieva-roc-drugs-test-olympics-spt-intl-hnk/index.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

On February 14, the [[Court of Arbitration for Sport]] (CAS) ruled that Valieva be allowed to compete in the [[Figure skating at the 2022 Winter Olympics – Women's singles|individual women's event]], on grounds that preventing her from competing "would cause her irreparable harm in the circumstances",<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Ellingworth|first=James|last2=Dunbar|first2=Graham|date=14 February 2022|title=Russian skater can compete, but medal ceremony won’t be held|url=https://apnews.com/article/winter-olympics-kamila-valieva-doping-decision-0dd063b5092681697525b69cd0c7212d|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250211090611/https://apnews.com/article/winter-olympics-kamila-valieva-doping-decision-0dd063b5092681697525b69cd0c7212d|archive-date=11 February 2025|access-date=30 December 2025|website=[[AP News]]|language=}}</ref> though her gold medal in the team event was still under consideration. The favorable decision from the Court was made in part due to her age, as minor athletes were subject to different rules than adult athletes.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{cite web |date=14 February 2022 |title=Olympic Winter Games Beijing 2022 (8) – The CAS Ad Hoc Division declines to impose a provisional suspension on the Russian figure skater Kamila Valieva |url=https://www.tas-cas.org/fileadmin/user_upload/CAS_Ad_Hoc_Media_Release_Beijing_8.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220214151257/https://www.tas-cas.org/fileadmin/user_upload/CAS_Ad_Hoc_Media_Release_Beijing_8.pdf |archive-date=14 February 2022 |access-date=15 February 2022 |website= |publisher=[[Court of Arbitration for Sport]]}}</ref> The IOC announced that the medal ceremony would not take place until the investigation was over and there was a concrete decision of whether to strip Russia of their medals.<ref>{{cite web |date=14 February 2022 |title=IOC EB decides no medal ceremonies following CAS decision on the case of ROC skater |url=https://olympics.com/ioc/news/ioc-eb-decides-no-medal-ceremonies-following-cas-decision-on-the-case-of-roc-skater |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220214101407/https://olympics.com/ioc/news/ioc-eb-decides-no-medal-ceremonies-following-cas-decision-on-the-case-of-roc-skater |archive-date=14 February 2022 |access-date=30 December 2025 |website=[[International Olympic Committee]]}}</ref>

On January 29, 2024, the CAS disqualified Valieva for four years retroactive to 25 December 2021 for the positive test for trimetazidine, which they ruled constituted an anti-doping rule violation.<ref name="Valieva12">{{cite web |date=29 January 2024 |title=Kamila Valieva is found to have committed an anti-doping rule violation and sanctioned with a four-year period of ineligibility commencing on 25 December 2021 |url=https://www.tas-cas.org/fileadmin/user_upload/CAS_Media_Release_9451_9455_9456_Decision.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240130172848/https://www.tas-cas.org/fileadmin/user_upload/CAS_Media_Release_9451_9455_9456_Decision.pdf |archive-date=30 January 2024 |access-date=29 January 2024 |website= |publisher=[[Court of Arbitration for Sport]]}}</ref> On 30 January 2024, the ISU, among other actions, subtracted Valieva's points from Russia's score without changing any other scores, and re-allocated the medals in the figure skating team event, upgrading the United States and Japan to gold and silver, respectively, while downgrading Russia to bronze.<ref name="ISUReranking2">{{cite web |date=30 January 2024 |title=ISU Statement – Decision of CAS – Kamila Valieva (ROC) |url=https://www.isu.org/isu-news/news/145-news/14898-isu-statement-decision-of-cas-kamila-valieva-roc2?templateParam=15 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240504025723/https://isu.org/isu-news/news/145-news/14898-isu-statement-decision-of-cas-kamila-valieva-roc2?templateParam=15 |archive-date=4 May 2024 |access-date=4 May 2024 |website=[[International Skating Union]]}}</ref> The American and Japanese teams ultimately received their medals at a ceremony which took place on 7 August 2024 at the [[Jardins du Trocadéro]] during the [[2024 Summer Olympics]] in [[Paris]].<ref>{{cite web |date=7 August 2024 |title=Figure Skating Team Event medalists from Beijing 2022 Olympic Winter Games honored in Paris |url=https://www.isu.org/isu-news/news/145-news/15036-figure-skating-team-event-medalists-from-beijing-2022-olympic-winter-games-honored-in-paris?templateParam=15 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240808165039/https://www.isu.org/isu-news/news/145-news/15036-figure-skating-team-event-medalists-from-beijing-2022-olympic-winter-games-honored-in-paris |archive-date=8 August 2024 |access-date=8 August 2024 |website=[[International Skating Union]]}}</ref>

==Skaters who won multiple Olympic medals==
[[File:2011 Four Continents Tessa VIRTUE Scott MOIR 3.jpg|thumb|upright=0.9|alt=Ice dancers Tessa Virtue and Scott Moir dancing on ice together.|[[Tessa Virtue]] and [[Scott Moir]] of Canada are the most decorated Olympic figure skaters, having won a total of five medals.]]
[[File:Marina Klimova and Sergei Ponomarenko.jpg|thumb|upright=0.9|alt=An ice dance couple performing a routine. The man, on the right, is dressed with a dark suit and holds his white-dressed partner by her waist and left hand.|[[Marina Klimova]] and [[Sergei Ponomarenko]] of the Soviet Union won bronze medals in 1984, silver in 1988, and gold in 1992.]]

===Multiple gold medals===
[[File:Bundesarchiv Bild 102-12803, Gilles Grafström.jpg|thumb|upright=0.9|right|alt=A male figure skater looks at the camera while performing a figure skating element on an outdoor ice rink.|Swedish [[Gillis Grafström]] is a three-time Olympic figure skating gold medalist in the men's singles event.]]
The only skaters with three consecutive titles are [[Gillis Grafström]] in men's singles, [[Sonja Henie]] in women's singles, and [[Irina Rodnina]] in pairs. The most consecutive titles in ice dance is two, which has only been achieved by [[Oksana Grishuk]] and [[Evgeny Platov]]. In addition, one women's singles skater, three men's singles skaters, and five pair skaters have earned consecutive titles. Two ice dancers and three pair skaters have earned non-consecutive titles.

Six skaters have won Olympic gold medals in multiple events. [[Evgeni Plushenko]] won gold in men's singles in 2006 and team event gold in 2014. [[Tatiana Volosozhar]] and [[Maxim Trankov]] were the first skaters to win multiple events at a single Olympics, winning in both pairs and the team event. [[Tessa Virtue]] and [[Scott Moir]] matched this feat four years later, earning golds in ice dance and the team event. [[Nathan Chen]] won gold in both men's singles and the team event in 2022.

=== Multiple Olympic medals by event ===
==== Men's singles ====
[[File:Karl_Schaefer_1935_by_Karl_Schleich.jpg|thumb|upright=0.9|right|alt=Male figure skater performing a jump|[[Karl Schäfer (figure skater)|Karl Schäfer]] of Austria won two Olympic gold medals in the men's competition in the 1930s.]]
[[File:2018_Winter_Olympics_-_Yuzuru_Hanyu_SP.jpg|thumb|upright=0.9|right|alt=Male figure skater on the ice|[[Yuzuru Hanyu]] of Japan is one of only two skaters to win two Olympic gold medals in the men's competition after [[World War II]].]]

====Women's singles====
[[File:Bundesarchiv Bild 102-09482, Sonja Henie.jpg|thumb|upright=0.9|right|alt=A young smiling woman wearing an embroidered hat and a jacket with furred collar and sleeve hems.|Norwegian [[Sonja Henie]] won three consecutive gold medals in the women's individual event (1928–1936).]]
[[File:Bundesarchiv Bild 183-1988-0105-018, Katarina Witt.jpg|thumb|upright=0.9|right|alt=A young smiling woman wearing a traditional Spanish flamenco dress and head gear, and executing the typical flamenco posture.|[[Katarina Witt]] from East Germany won the 1988 women's singles gold medal, becoming the second female figure skater in history to win back-to-back Olympic titles.]]
[[File:Yunakimedal2.jpg|thumb|upright=0.9|right|alt=Female figure skater showing her gold medal|[[Yuna Kim]] of South Korea won the women's singles event in 2010 with world record scores in the short program, free skating, and combined total.]]

===Multiple disciplines===
[[File:Beatrix Loughran LOC.jpg|thumb|upright=0.9|right|alt=A young smiling woman wearing a fur coat waving.|[[Beatrix Loughran]] of the United States won two Olympic medals in [[single skating|women's singles]] and one in [[pair skating]].]]
Only three skaters have won Olympic medals in multiple [[Figure skating#Disciplines|figure skating disciplines]]. In 1908, [[Madge Syers]] of Great Britain became the first skater to medal in multiple figure skating disciplines at a single Olympics. The only skater to match this feat was [[Ernst Baier]] of Germany in 1936. [[Beatrix Loughran]] of the United States won a silver medal in [[Single skating|women's singles]] at the [[1924 Winter Olympics]], a bronze medal in women's singles at the [[1928 Winter Olympics]], and a silver medal in [[pair skating]] at the [[1932 Winter Olympics]].<ref name="BeatrixLoughran" />
